text: My eyes grew wide as though seeking the comfort of my brow from as much amazement as much fear at my grandmother's voice.
"Kali", she said. "Her skin darker than the deep night, eyes as red as the setting sun, a gushing river made hair, the very fury of nature bound human", she sighed, "Kali faced one final challenge".
Quite a storyteller she was and oh, how the old woman loved metaphors.
The story was a bribe for getting me to eat my dinner and like all her stories, this one too was supernatural, mythical and fantasy filled.
The story must have begun along the lines of a demon-king ruling over the world and a prophecy-born Kali, the world's savior come to rescue them after much suffering.
"Kali's final challenge was the King himself", she continued. "The King didn't look fearsome like what you would expect of a demon, in fact he looked very much human.

But Kali who could see beneath the mantle knew better; for this self-proclaimed king was a skilled sorcerer, the darkest and cruelest at that, a sorcerer who could live a thousand lives and not age a day, a tyrant who rejoiced at the suffering of the weak, how terrible..., that is very fearsome, no?", she asked.
I blinked, nodded and looked on. It was her cue to keep going.

"Kali was the supreme incarnate and no less extraordinary", her voice now seemed to carry a certainty that mere grammar couldn't convey, "Kali had a unique power, she could create anything just by thinking it, she herself was indeed a manifestation of the supreme thought".
She paused, "the silence between Kali and the king seemed to stretch forever, or perhaps the voices of their hostility were so loud that mere humans like us couldn't perceive.
As a wicked smile etched across his thin, pale lips, Kali knew it was past time to do what she must have done a long time ago - to end the life of this tyrant".

My grandmother's ancient eyes glistened at something very distant, "Kali knew the power of his sorcery, the magic that made him immune to earthly weapons was like nothing she had known to be possible, death was but a feeble servant of the king.

She closed her eyes in a calculating thought, muttered something strange under her breath, her eyes flew open and her whispers now seemed to be all around like they were always there, the wind around her wore a new face, wielding an unnatural power.

As though in response, the king's voice rose with every gust of the wind, speaking an ancient tongue long forgotten, his voice turned hoarse and an invisible dome seemed to form around him holding Kali at bay, the world around them seemed to wither as he drew his power from everything around.

Kali realized keeping at this might just as well lead to the destruction of life around her, she stopped for a brief moment, a quick thought crossed her mind, and a fierce weapon formed in thin air before her and fell into her waiting hands".

My grandmother drew a deep breath, smiled and said, "Oh, the weapon she conjured was magnificent, forged from the sinew of a very powerful being that existed before time itself - it could sever anything, physical or otherwise.

Before the king could even draw on his next breath, Kali swung her weapon in a wide arc at the foe cutting through his flesh, bone and the sorcery that bound him human, severing him into a million pieces as the field around her turned dark with his blood".
I took a deep breath, but something told me it wasn't over yet and as if echoing my thoughts, my grandmother shook her head.

"Oh, that wasn't the end of him, the king in his infinite guile may have anticipated this, for the anger, surprise and perhaps even despair in Kali's eyes spoke volumes of the horror that unfolded before her.

Every drop of the sorcerer's blood that was spilled seemed to have a will of its own drawing mass from nowhere and everywhere, each drop of the blood shaped itself to look like the king, it was like looking at the sorcerer in a million mirrors, only they weren't mere reflections.

The king's magic ran wild a million times over and there was only so much she could do against the overwhelming army of madmen closing in on her; she conjured up a shield and hoped it would hold. Kali was perplexed and knew there was very little time before her sanctuary would give way".
My grandmother paused, ruffled my hair as though urging me not to despair.

She cracked her knuckles and said, "Clarity dawned upon Kali as she realized that the king had perhaps cursed his own blood to cheat his death and she couldn't afford another cut at him, her thoughts roared like a raging ocean and the solution hit her like a tiny rock caught amidst the waves.

She had no time to lose. Kali began to grow towards the heavens stepping out of her shield, the enormity of her form could only be measured by the  fear reflected in a million eyes of the sorcerer. One of Kali's hand alone could block out the skies of a hundred worlds".

The wonder in my eyes painted my grandmother's words with a smile, "Like a giant net trapping a thousand trout, Kali grabbed at the whole encroaching army and swallowed them down her immense gut all in a single gulp.
You see, Kali was but Thought-made-human and she knew the king's sorcery would be lost in the abyss of her nature.
The duel was over just like that, the king's fall brought a great joy to the world. The magic he had woven that enslaved the world vanished with him.

The smell of freedom told Kali that her purpose there was fulfilled. She resumed her normal form, spared a fleeting glance around and stepped into the mists of air to become one with it like she was never there".
My grandmother's wide grin announced the end of the story.
As I think, it was as much her success as much as Kali's for my dinner plate was clean; vegetables, greens and all gone.
